title: Incremental Repo Review V1
description: repo-review needs a durable incremental review workflow for packages that have already received a full review. Oathweaver and OverCR are active target packages whose maintainer wants a CLI-driven maintenance workflow sooner than originally expected. The work must preserve staged review discipline while adding claim/evidence state, delta review, Drift Surfacer updates, and a narrow agent-native CLI slice.
design: Deliver v1 as a staged program of work: design the incremental substrate, validate it with schemas and calibration, build a narrow agent-native CLI slice, prove delta review on one active package, then harden the framework. Keep the first CLI surface small but enforce agent-native behavior from the first shipped command.
acceptance_criteria:
- Incremental review substrate is documented and calibrated.
- Review state, claims, evidence, diff reports, impact plans, and delta Drift Surfacer outputs have initial schemas or documented shapes.
- A narrow CLI slice exposes agent-context, skill-path, status, profiles, and feedback with agent-native behavior.
- A delta vertical slice can generate a diff report, impact plan, prompt packet, and delta review artifact for Oathweaver or OverCR.
- CLI behavior is enforced with automated tests for non-interactive execution, parseable JSON, actionable errors, bounded output, and vocabulary consistency.

title: Design incremental review substrate
description: repo-review needs a precise design for incremental review before implementation can safely encode assumptions. The design must define full and delta modes, durable review state, claims, evidence, analyzer identity, drift handling, impact planning, Drift Surfacer integration, framework limits, and the agent-native CLI contract.
design: Create `docs/incremental-review.md` as the canonical engineering spec. Include concrete YAML/JSON-like shapes for the durable substrate and enough CLI contract detail for later implementation. The document should be practical and implementable, not an essay.
acceptance_criteria:
- `docs/incremental-review.md` exists.
- The document defines full and delta modes.
- The document defines review state, claim/evidence, diff report, impact plan, analyzer identity, contested claim, and delta Drift Surfacer shapes.
- The document defines claim ID scoping and collision behavior.
- The document separates watch-path impact matches from invalidation-trigger evaluation.
- The document defines agent-native CLI requirements, including agent-context, skill-path, profiles, feedback, vocabulary policy, exit codes, and bounded output.
- The document names framework limits and calibration criteria.

title: Write incremental review design doc
description: The project needs a canonical in-repo design document for incremental review so later tooling has a stable target. Without this document, implementation would encode unsettled planning assumptions in code.
design: Create `docs/incremental-review.md`. Cover goals/non-goals, full vs delta modes, review state, claim rubric, claim/evidence schema, analyzer identity, conflation guard, diff report schema, open diff taxonomy, impact planner schema, Drift Surfacer integration, agent-native CLI contract, framework limits, and calibration criteria.
acceptance_criteria:
- `docs/incremental-review.md` contains all Phase 0 topics.
- The document uses concrete structured examples rather than only prose.
- The document is sufficient for a future agent to implement validators and the first CLI slice without reading planning chat history.

title: Define claim and evidence substrate
description: Delta review needs durable claims and evidence references that survive across repo versions and analyzer sessions. The framework needs a small but real claim shape before calibration or impact planning can be meaningful.
design: Define the claim rubric, claim status vocabulary, evidence references, analyzer identity fields, claim ID scoping, contested claims, dependencies, related claims, watch paths, and invalidation triggers. Use semantic claim IDs scoped to the containing `review_state.id`; cross-review references use `<review_state_id>:<claim_id>`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Claim rubric includes inclusion and exclusion rules.
- Claim status vocabulary includes active, superseded, contested, and invalidated.
- Claim IDs are scoped to `review_state.id`, with collision behavior documented.
- Evidence refs, analyzer identity, `contested_by`, `watch_paths`, and `invalidation_triggers` are documented.
- The design distinguishes repo claims about itself from analyst claims about the repo.

title: Define diff and impact schemas
description: Delta review needs a disciplined way to map repository changes to likely affected claims. Simple file matching is not enough because prose invalidation triggers may catch subtle subject drift outside watched paths.
design: Define git diff report, open diff taxonomy, impact plan, `path_hits`, `trigger_hits`, `impacted_claims`, `unaffected_claims`, and `unknowns`. Built-in classifications should coexist with project-local classifications, and unknown categories should be treated conservatively.
acceptance_criteria:
- Diff report schema includes repo, commits/range, changed files, and classifications.
- Impact plan schema separates `path_hits`, `trigger_hits`, `impacted_claims`, `unaffected_claims`, and `unknowns`.
- Open diff taxonomy has built-ins and permits project-local categories.
- Invalidation trigger evaluation is explicitly analyst/LLM-evaluated, not treated as decorative prose.

title: Specify agent-native CLI contract
description: The first repo-review CLI slice will be used by agents and by active package maintainers. It needs explicit behavior contracts from the start so the CLI does not hang, emit brittle output, duplicate work on retry, or drift from conventional command vocabulary.
design: Specify CLI requirements for non-interactive execution, `--json` stdout/stderr separation, actionable errors with enumerated valid values, safe mutation boundaries, bounded responses, vocabulary policy, exit code taxonomy, `agent-context`, `skill-path`, profile model, feedback log, delivery schemes, and conditional jobs/`--wait` behavior. Define a command registry/schema approach so help text, agent-context, examples, and vocabulary checks can be generated or validated from one source.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLI contract defines `--no-input` as the canonical headless flag.
- CLI contract defines exit codes 0 through 7.
- CLI contract defines `agent-context` and `skill-path` output expectations.
- CLI contract defines profile precedence: explicit flag > environment variable > profile > default.
- CLI contract defines feedback storage behavior.
- CLI contract defines vocabulary policy and banned aliases.
- CLI contract states when jobs and `--wait` are required or deferred.

title: Document framework limits and calibration criteria
description: The framework needs explicit limits and calibration criteria so users know what incremental review can and cannot prove. Calibration must be allowed to revise the substrate if structure distorts review judgment.
design: Add framework limits to `docs/incremental-review.md`, including context contamination, training-data contamination, analyzer/model differences, source-only review limits, generated/vendor ambiguity, curator/author/analyzer overlap, stale prior reviews, and contradictory analyst outputs. Add calibration questions that test whether claims/evidence preserve prose judgment and support future delta review.
acceptance_criteria:
- Framework limits are explicitly listed.
- Calibration criteria test methodology, not only schema parsing.
- Calibration findings are allowed to revise Phase 0 substrate decisions through the decision log.

title: Validate substrate and seed CLI
description: The incremental review substrate needs minimal validators, one calibration review, and a narrow agent-native CLI slice before delta review work depends on it. This phase tests both data shape and workflow ergonomics.
design: Add schema files, a frontmatter linter, output validation, a minimal CLI harness, CLI agent-readiness tests, one calibration review, and useful fixtures from existing self-review outputs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Initial schemas or documented structured shapes exist.
- Existing pass frontmatter can be linted.
- At least one pass output shape can be validated.
- Minimal CLI exposes `agent-context`, `skill-path`, `status`, profile commands, and `feedback`.
- CLI agent-readiness tests are automated.
- One calibration review produces lessons and decision-log updates.

title: Add initial review schemas
description: Validators and CLI commands need shared structured contracts for review state, claims, diff reports, impact plans, and delta Drift Surfacer output. Without initial schemas, each tool will invent its own shape.
design: Create an initial `schemas/` directory or equivalent documented schema files for `review_state`, `claim`, `diff_report`, `impact_plan`, and `delta_drift`. Keep schemas strict enough to catch missing required fields but flexible enough to evolve after calibration.
acceptance_criteria:
- Schemas or structured shape files exist for `review_state`, `claim`, `diff_report`, `impact_plan`, and `delta_drift`.
- Required fields match `docs/incremental-review.md`.
- Schemas support analyzer identity and claim status vocabulary.

title: Implement pass frontmatter linter
description: repo-review pass files declare prerequisites and output metadata in frontmatter, but those declarations are not mechanically checked. A linter is needed to catch missing or malformed pass metadata before orchestration depends on it.
design: Add a linter for pass frontmatter. Validate required keys, known pass IDs, output declaration shape, prerequisite references, and any new incremental metadata added by Phase 0.
acceptance_criteria:
- Linter can be run locally.
- Linter reports malformed pass frontmatter with actionable errors.
- Linter has at least one passing and one failing fixture.

title: Validate one pass output shape
description: The framework needs proof that a pass output can be checked against the new structured expectations. This should be a narrow validation path before broad orchestration.
design: Pick one existing pass output shape and validate it against the schema or structured contract. Prefer an existing repo-review self-review output as a fixture if available.
acceptance_criteria:
- One pass output fixture validates successfully.
- At least one malformed output fixture fails with a useful message.
- The validation path can be reused by later CLI commands.

title: Build minimal CLI registry and introspection
description: The first CLI slice should be small but introspectable. Agents need a stable way to discover commands, flags, enum values, schemas, output paths, and vocabulary policy without scraping prose documentation.
design: Implement a minimal repo-review CLI harness with a central command registry. Ship `repo-review agent-context --json` and `repo-review skill-path --json`. `agent-context` should include `schema_version`, command names, flags, enum values, output schemas where practical, supported delivery schemes, available profiles, skill manifest path, and vocabulary policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- `repo-review agent-context --json` returns valid JSON with `schema_version`.
- `agent-context` lists shipped commands, flags, enums, and vocabulary policy.
- `repo-review skill-path --json` returns an existing directory containing a readable task manifest.
- Machine-mode output emits JSON on stdout and diagnostics on stderr.

title: Add profile status and feedback commands
description: Oathweaver and OverCR review work will repeat across sessions. Agents and humans need persistent defaults, compact status, and a way to record CLI friction without relying on chat memory.
design: Implement `repo-review status --json`, `repo-review profile list|show|save|delete --json`, and `repo-review feedback "..." --json`. Profiles should capture repo root, review output directory, analyzer identity, lane vocabulary path, and preferred output mode. Use precedence explicit flag > environment variable > profile > default. Feedback writes local JSONL and returns entry id/path.
acceptance_criteria:
- `status --json` reports configured paths, available profiles, and next relevant review actions.
- Profile commands support JSON output and no-input behavior.
- Feedback command records entries durably and returns the stored entry path/id.
- Explicit flags override environment variables, which override profiles, which override defaults.

title: Add agent-native CLI tests
description: Agent-native behavior must be enforced by tests from the first CLI slice. Otherwise later commands can accidentally add prompts, unparseable output, inconsistent vocabulary, or unsafe mutation defaults.
design: Add tests for no prompts in machine mode, valid JSON stdout, diagnostics on stderr, no color/spinners in JSON mode, actionable error shape, bounded output behavior, vocabulary consistency, profile precedence, and no implicit overwrite/destructive mutation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests fail if a JSON command prints non-JSON on stdout.
- Tests fail if machine mode can prompt for input.
- Tests cover actionable errors with code, message, hint, and enumerated valid values where applicable.
- Tests cover approved command/flag vocabulary and banned aliases.
- Tests cover safe mutation boundaries such as `--overwrite`, `--force`, and `--dry-run`.

title: Run full calibration review
description: The claim/evidence substrate must be tested against a real repo before it drives Oathweaver or OverCR delta work. Calibration needs to reveal whether the structured substrate preserves expert review judgment or distorts it.
design: Run a fresh full review against a small but non-trivial package using the updated substrate. Produce a review state, claims, evidence, and Drift Surfacer output. Record whether the substrate helped or hurt analysis, then update the decision log if needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Calibration review produces a review state artifact.
- Claims and evidence can be inspected without reading the full prose review.
- Calibration notes identify substrate changes or confirm no changes are needed.
- Any substrate change is reflected in docs and schemas.

title: Convert self-review outputs into fixtures
description: Existing repo-review self-review outputs can provide realistic fixtures for validators and CLI tests. This reduces artificial examples and helps catch workflow drift.
design: Identify existing self-review outputs, select stable examples, and convert them into fixtures for frontmatter linting, pass output validation, review state parsing, and delta prompt generation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixture files are added or documented.
- Fixtures cover at least one valid and one invalid validation path.
- Fixture provenance is clear enough for future updates.

title: Build delta review vertical slice
description: The v1 workflow needs a working end-to-end delta review path over one active package. The slice should produce a diff report, impact plan, prompt packet, delta review artifact, and delta Drift Surfacer output without attempting full orchestration.
design: Implement commands and artifacts for diff report, impact planning, prompt export, and delta Drift Surfacer output. Run the slice on Oathweaver or OverCR using a prior review state.
acceptance_criteria:
- One active package can be processed through the delta slice.
- Each produced artifact is inspectable and parseable.
- The slice preserves claim/evidence continuity from the prior review state.
- CLI commands used in the slice obey the agent-native contract.

title: Implement git diff report command
description: Delta review starts with a structured report of repository changes. Agents need this as JSON rather than ad hoc `git diff` summarization.
design: Implement `repo-review diff --json --no-input`. Support explicit range input, path filters, bounded output, and open classification support. The command should return changed files, summary stats, diff range, classification candidates, and truncation/narrowing hints when output is bounded.
acceptance_criteria:
- Command accepts an explicit git range.
- Command returns valid JSON with changed files and summary stats.
- Bounded output includes truncation metadata and narrowing hints.
- The command does not prompt in machine mode.

title: Implement impact planner command
description: Delta review needs to determine which durable claims are likely affected by a repo change. The impact planner must preserve the distinction between path matches, semantic invalidation-trigger matches, and unknowns.
design: Implement `repo-review impact --json`. Read review state and diff report, then produce `path_hits`, `trigger_hits`, `impacted_claims`, `unaffected_claims`, and `unknowns`. Use deterministic `watch_path` matching first; use analyst/LLM-evaluated trigger data if available; keep uncertain mappings visible.
acceptance_criteria:
- Command reads a review state and diff report.
- Output separates path hits, trigger hits, impacted claims, unaffected claims, and unknowns.
- Output explains why each impacted claim was surfaced.
- Unknowns are not silently dropped.

title: Export delta prompt packet
description: Agents need a low-token prompt packet that includes prior review state, diff report, impact plan, and instructions for updating affected claims without rerunning a full review.
design: Implement `repo-review export-prompt --pass delta-trace --output <path> --json --no-input`. Define overwrite behavior, dry-run behavior, and optional delivery sinks. The generated prompt should preserve the conflation guard and require analyzer identity in the output.
acceptance_criteria:
- Command writes a prompt packet to the requested path.
- Existing output paths require `--overwrite`.
- `--dry-run` reports the intended output path and required inputs without writing.
- Prompt includes prior review state, diff report, impact plan, and conflation guard instructions.

title: Add delta Drift Surfacer output
description: Drift Surfacer needs a delta form that can express new, invalidated, strengthened, and weakened observations without pretending a delta review is a full fresh review.
design: Define and test `delta_drift` output with repo, from_review, to_review, diff_range, produced_by_analyzer, new_snapshot_entries, invalidated_snapshot_entries, strengthened_fascination_seeds, weakened_fascination_seeds, new_fascination_seeds, and lane_impacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- `delta_drift` schema or structured shape exists.
- Output can represent new, invalidated, strengthened, and weakened material.
- Output includes analyzer identity.
- Output is tied to the diff range and prior review state.

title: Run delta slice on active package
description: The delta workflow must be proven on either Oathweaver or OverCR because those are the motivating packages and the maintainer wants a CLI-driven workflow soon.
design: Locate or create a prior full review state for either Oathweaver or OverCR. Run the diff report, impact planner, prompt export, external analysis step if needed, and delta Drift Surfacer update. Record friction as feedback entries or follow-up issues.
acceptance_criteria:
- Delta workflow runs on one active package.
- Delta workflow produces diff report, impact plan, prompt packet, delta review artifact, and `delta_drift` output.
- The run identifies any CLI or substrate gaps before broader expansion.

title: Expand agent-native CLI surface
description: After the substrate and delta vertical slice work, repo-review needs a broader composable CLI surface for agents and package maintainers. Expansion should keep vocabulary, introspection, profiles, bounded output, and safe mutation behavior consistent.
design: Add commands for next action selection, ingestion, delta orchestration, claims inspection, async job handling if needed, and delivery sinks. Keep the central command registry as the source of truth.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLI command set expands without violating the agent-native contract.
- `agent-context` remains complete and current.
- Tests enforce vocabulary and output consistency across the expanded command set.

title: Add next ingest and delta commands
description: Agents need higher-level commands after the low-level delta slice works. These commands should remain composable and inspectable rather than hiding all review judgment inside automation.
design: Implement `repo-review next --json`, `ingest --json`, and `delta --json`. `next` returns the next action, required inputs, missing inputs, output path, and recommended command. `ingest` validates and records external analyzer outputs. `delta` either executes analysis or assembles prompt packets depending on the Phase 2 decision.
acceptance_criteria:
- `next --json` returns actionable next-step data.
- `ingest --json` validates external analyzer output and records it.
- `delta --json` reflects the selected v1 orchestration model.
- Whether `repo-review delta` executes analysis itself determines jobs/`--wait` requirements.

title: Add claims CLI commands
description: Claims are the durable review substrate, so agents need direct query commands instead of parsing review-state files manually.
design: Implement `repo-review claims list --json`, `repo-review claims get <id> --json`, and `repo-review claims affected --json`. Support filters for claim_status, kind, subject, and limit. Use fully qualified claim IDs when crossing review states.
acceptance_criteria:
- `claims list` supports filters and bounded output.
- `claims get` retrieves one claim with evidence refs.
- `claims affected` reports claims from an impact plan.
- Commands use scoped claim IDs consistently.

title: Decide and implement async job strategy
description: If repo-review runs long analysis itself, agents need recoverable execution rather than hand-rolled polling. If repo-review only assembles prompt packets in v1, job commands should be deferred explicitly.
design: Decide whether v1 delta commands execute analysis or only assemble prompt packets. If analysis execution ships, implement `--wait` plus a durable local job ledger and `repo-review jobs list|get|prune --json`. If execution is deferred, document the deferral and omit jobs from the shipped command set.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision is documented in the CLI contract and command registry.
- If jobs ship, job commands return parseable JSON and stable IDs.
- If jobs are deferred, `agent-context` does not advertise unsupported job commands.

title: Add delivery sinks for artifacts
description: Some agent workflows need artifacts on stdout, some need files, and some may later need webhook delivery. Delivery behavior should be explicit and consistent.
design: Add `--deliver=stdout|file:<path>|webhook:<url>` where useful. Keep defaults conservative, avoid implicit overwrites, and return delivery metadata in JSON.
acceptance_criteria:
- Delivery schemes are documented in `agent-context`.
- File delivery requires explicit overwrite behavior for existing paths.
- Stdout delivery remains parseable in JSON mode.
- Webhook delivery is implemented or explicitly deferred.

title: Harden repo-review framework
description: After the incremental substrate and delta workflow are useful, repo-review needs documentation accuracy, helper templates, aggregation support, and extractable patterns to reduce confusion and improve repeated use.
design: Update public docs to match implemented behavior, add self-review hygiene, add helper templates, prototype aggregation over structured review state, and document validated reusable patterns.
acceptance_criteria:
- README reflects implemented behavior rather than aspirational workflow.
- Self-review hygiene exists for repo-review changes.
- Helper templates reduce repeated manual work.
- Aggregation prototype works over v1 review states.
- Extractable patterns are documented only after real use.

title: Rewrite README for implemented behavior
description: The README should describe what repo-review actually supports after v1, not the broader conceptual ambition. Accurate docs matter more once external users are interested in the CLI.
design: Rewrite README sections for workflow, CLI usage, artifact model, full vs delta review, limitations, and example runs. Keep conceptual framing concise and put operational details first.
acceptance_criteria:
- README names implemented commands and artifacts accurately.
- README distinguishes full review, delta review, and non-goals.
- README includes a minimal CLI example for agents and humans.

title: Add repo-review self-review hygiene
description: Once incremental review exists, repo-review should use its own delta workflow when the framework changes. Without self-review hygiene, changes to the review method can drift without durable review memory.
design: Document when repo-review changes should trigger incremental self-review, what artifacts should be updated, and how to avoid contaminating calibration with self-referential review unless intentionally testing the framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Self-review trigger criteria are documented.
- Required artifacts for framework changes are documented.
- Guidance distinguishes calibration from routine self-review.

title: Add review helper templates
description: Repeated repo-review use will benefit from helper materials that make trace, lift, and twin selection more consistent without adding new analysis passes.
design: Add helper templates for common review decisions, such as selecting affected claims, writing invalidation triggers, summarizing drift, and recording contested claims.
acceptance_criteria:
- Helper templates exist for recurring v1 review tasks.
- Templates are referenced from docs or CLI output where useful.
- Helpers reduce repeated work without expanding the core pass set prematurely.

title: Prototype cross-review aggregation
description: As repo-review produces more structured claims and drift material, users will need ways to compare or aggregate outputs across reviews without modeling cross-repo claim relationships in v1.
design: Prototype aggregation over review states, claim statuses, analyzer identities, diff outcomes, and Drift Surfacer outputs. Keep cross-repo claim identity out of scope unless a later plan explicitly adds it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Aggregation prototype can read multiple review states.
- Output summarizes claim statuses, analyzer identities, and drift material.
- Output does not imply unsupported cross-repo claim identity.

title: Document extractable review patterns
description: Some repo-review patterns may be reusable outside this project, but only patterns validated by real use should be documented as extractables.
design: Identify validated reusable patterns from the incremental review work and document them as extractables. Candidate patterns include enforcement tracing and delta-as-finding, but include only patterns that survived real use.
acceptance_criteria:
- Extractables are based on validated workflow evidence.
- Each extractable explains the reusable pattern and when to apply it.
- Documentation avoids presenting speculative patterns as proven.
